method: Curated comparison of explicit removal deadlines and qualitative response standards found in official primary or regulator sources. Absence from this file does not mean that a jurisdiction has no removal duty.

entries.trigger: After an eSafety removal notice is given
entries.actor: Online service, hosting provider, or end user named in the notice
entries.scope: Image-based abuse and other material covered by the Online Safety Act schemes
entries.required_action: Take all reasonable steps to remove or cease hosting the material
entries.instrument: Online Safety Act 2021 — Image-Based Abuse Scheme
entries.note: eSafety may specify a longer period in the notice.

entries.trigger: After a covered platform receives a valid removal request
entries.scope: Nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including qualifying digital forgeries
entries.required_action: Remove the reported depiction and make reasonable efforts to remove known identical copies
entries.instrument: TAKE IT DOWN Act, Pub. L. 119-12
entries.source_title: FTC: Complying With the TAKE IT DOWN Act
entries.note: The FTC began enforcing the platform notice-and-removal requirements on May 19, 2026.

entries.trigger: After obtaining actual knowledge or awareness of illegal content
entries.scope: Illegal content under applicable Union or Member State law
entries.required_action: Remove or disable access expeditiously to retain the hosting liability exemption
entries.note: The DSA provision uses a qualitative standard rather than a universal fixed-hour deadline.
